03 MEASURED EVIDENCE

Two baselines,
one honest conclusion.

Classic SIFT tests reproducibility; SuperPoint + LightGlue tests whether stronger cross-domain matching changes the feasibility verdict.

BASELINE A · CLASSIC COLMAP

SIFT failed to bridge eras.

The selected joint component contained modern cameras only. A low reprojection error did not rescue the missing historical connection.

BASELINE B · HLOC + COLMAP

Learned features recovered camera connectivity.

NetVLAD, SuperPoint, and LightGlue found genuine cross-era constraints. The stricter question remains whether enough Boardman-only structure survived to support a surface.

05 METHOD
  1. 01

    Acquire

    Query Commons for Boardman, Uris, and McGraw; filter license and metadata; hash every accepted file.

    ONLINE
  2. 02

    Retrieve + match

    Rank image overlap with NetVLAD, extract SuperPoint features, match with LightGlue, and verify geometry in COLMAP.

    HLOC
  3. 03

    Joint reconstruction

    Estimate cameras and sparse tracks with COLMAP; count cross-era tracks and Boardman-only multiview tracks separately.

    SFM
  4. 04

    Dense release gate

    Require target-specific support and a validated dense surface. On this machine, COLMAP PatchMatch is also blocked because the installed build has no CUDA.

    FAIL CLOSED
V1 CONCLUSION
Registration improved.
Recovery did not pass.

The correct output under the zero-human-in-the-loop constraint is a negative feasibility result—not a prettier fake.
